### L-T-P FORMAT 2-0-2

### COURSE SUMMARY

This course introduces the fundamentals and advanced concepts of AI -powered UAV systems, covering

core UAV components, flight dynamics, and perception sensors. Students learn UAV simulation (Gazebo,

AirSim) and ROS 2 middleware for autonomy. AI -driven perception topics include computer vision,

object detection, tracking, segmentation, and SLAM/VIO for localization. Path planning methods (A*,

RRT, potential fields) and obstacle avoidance strategies enable autonomous navigation. High -level

mission control is explored through state machines, behavior trees, and layered software architectures. The

course also covers multi -UAV coordination, communication protocols, safety regulations, and emerging

applications, building a strong foundation for UAV research and real-world deployments.

### COURSE-SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (CO)

By the end of this program, students should have the following knowledge, skills and values:

CO1: Understand the core concepts of UAV systems, their components, flight dynamics, and the role of AI

in UAV applications.

CO2: Apply AI and computer vision techniques for perception, mapping, and localization in UAVs.

CO3: Design autonomous navigation strategies and path planning algorithms for UAVs in dynamic

environments.

CO4: Develop intelligent decision-making systems and understand communication, regulation, and

coordination in multi-UAV operations.

### DETAILED SYLLABUS

### UNIT I (Contact hours: 7)

AI in UAVs: Course Overview, Applications, and Ethical Considerations , UAV Types, UAV Flight Dynamics

and Control, Sensors for UAV Perception , Image Formation , LiDAR, IMU, GPS, Barometer, Sensor Fusion

Concepts, ROS 2: Architecture, Nodes, Topics, Services, Messages , UAV Simulation Environments: Gazebo and

AirSim, SITL/HITL

Unit II (Contact hours: 7)

Computer Vision for UAVs Feature Detection and Matching -SIFT, SURF, ORB, Object Detection Techniques -

e.g., YOLO in Aerial Imagery , Object Tracking Algorithms -e.g., DeepSORT and Challenges , Semantic and

Instance Segmentation for Scene Understanding, SLAM: SLAM Problem, Key Concepts -Localization, Mapping,

Loop Closure, Visual SLAM -V-SLAM: Feature-based vs. Direct Methods, Monocular vs. Stereo , Visual-Inertial

Odometry -VIO and SLAM: Sensor Fusion for Robust Localization.

Unit III (Contact hours: 4)

Path Planning Configuration Space, Grid -Based Methods -A*, Advanced Path Planning: Sampling -Based

Methods -RRT, RRT*, Potential Fields, Real-time Obstacle Detection and Avoidance: Sensor-based Techniques -

VFH, DWA, UAV Mission Control Architectures: Layered Software Stacks, Onboard Processing.

Unit IV Decision-Making and Mission Control

State Machines for UAV Task Management: Designing Mission Logic with FSMs , Behavior Trees for Complex

UAV Missions: Principles and Advantages over FSMs , Communication and Networking: MAVLink Protocol,

ROS 2 Communication -DDS, Multi-UAV Systems: Coordination Concepts and Challenges , UAV Regulations

and Safety: Airspace Rules -e.g., DGCA, Geofencing, Fail -Safes, Real-world Applications and Emerging

Technologies in AI-powered UAVs.

### LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS:

1.Development Environment Setup: Installing ROS 2, Gazebo/PX4 SITL, Python ROS 2

Publisher/Subscriber.

2. UAV Simulation: UAV Control -Takeoff, Landing, Waypoints in Gazebo/PX4 SITL using MAVROS

or PX4-ROS 2 Bridge.

3. Accessing Sensor Data: Reading IMU, GPS, and Camera Data from Simulated UAV via ROS 2 Topics.

4. Image Processing with OpenCV: Loading, Processing, and Displaying Images from UAV's Simulated

Camera Feed.

5. Object Detection on Aerial Images: Pre-trained Object Detector -e.g., YOLO via OpenCV DNN on

Simulated Camera Data.

6. Visual Feature Tracking: Implementing a Feature Tracker -e.g., KLT on Simulated Video Streams.

7. SLAM Implementation/Integration: Running V-SLAM Package -e.g., ORB-SLAM2/3 with Simulated

Sensor Data.

8.Path Planning Implementation -Grid-Based: A* Algorithm for 2D Grid Navigation in Python.

9. Path Planning Implementation -Sampling-Based: RRT for 2D Path Finding in Python.

10. Reactive Obstacle Avoidance Simulation: Potential Field or Bug Algorithm in Simulation.

11. Mission Control with State Machines/Behavior Trees: Mission Sequence -e.g., Takeoff-Waypoint-

Land using FSM or BT library in Python/ROS 2.

12. Combining elements for integrated task -e.g., fly to a point, detect an object, report.

Attendance Policy

1. At least 75% attendance in the course is mandatory

2. A maximum of 5% shall be allowed under medical grounds and 5% on representing the

University on official events outside like sports, hackathons, NCC, NSS etc.

3. Students with less than 65% of attendance shall be prevented from writing the final

assessment.

Academic Dishonesty & Plagiarism

Plagiarism is "to offer work or ideas from another source as one's own, with or without

authorization of the source author(s), directly by verbatim copying or by usage of any AI

software" (i.e., with or without permission from the original author). In certain cases,

authorization might be provided for the usage of other sources through written permission

may not be considered as plagiarism. It is a serious academic offence which should be

avoided, the following method will be adopted to evaluate plagiarism in submitted

documents including assignments, material, class test content and other similar academic
